quotes.text: Never color only. If an alert state is critical, bind an icon, an adjacent label or a pattern.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A compact accessibility rule: alerts need redundancy beyond color.

quotes.text: For text and UI labels, enforce a 4.51 contrast ratio minimum. For graphical marks, bars, lines, points, never under 3-1.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives concrete, testable contrast thresholds for report themes.

quotes.text: And here's the brutal rule. If a color tweak breaks brand brand yields. Data truth out ranks aesthetics. Always.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core principle that readability beats brand colors.

quotes.text: Hover, an outline or elevation change, not a color that mimics selected. Disabled, reduce opacity and drop saturation, but keep text legible at AA.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical guidance for distinguishable slicer states.

quotes.text: Your theme is the containment field. Govern it rootlessly or your data lies loudly and slowly. Adopt the validation report today.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's call to treat themes as governed assets.

chapters.title: Why Power BI themes can lie
Validation protocol, automation and version control

takeaways: Power BI themes are a governance layer: low contrast and undefined styles can hide alerts, subtotals, tooltips, card hierarchy and slicer states.
Define alert states, subtotal styles, tooltip elements, card ratios and all four slicer states explicitly in the theme JSON and test them against real backgrounds with pass/fail contrast thresholds.
Manage themes like code: validation report, version control with pull requests, signed organizational themes and blocked local overrides on certified workspaces.
hook: Brand colors in a Power BI theme can quietly bury alerts, erase subtotals and make slicer states impossible to read. This episode is for report creators and BI teams who want trustworthy dashboards, and it walks through five invisible theme failures plus a pass/fail validation protocol with contrast gates, JSON locks and organizational themes.
